lines.text: One agent sees every project, so it fixes the wrong one. Or nobody wakes it, and it does nothing.
A task manager for A I agents pushes the work. Here is how Agent R Q does it.
Every project gets its own workspace. Each card names its agent, green while it is connected.
Hand billing a task, and it goes straight to billing's agent.
No polling. Task latency is seconds, and an idle agent costs nothing.
The conversation is pushed too. Type while the agent works.
Your message reaches it mid-task. It answers, and keeps working.
Every task has one clear status: Not Started, Ongoing, Blocked or Done.
Switch tasks, and it starts fresh. Agent R Q runs slash clear in its terminal first.
And every workspace's tasks sit on one agent task board, live.
People get a task keyboard too. N for a new task, Command K to find one.
Does your agent wait for work, or get it pushed? Tell us in the comments. Agent R Q is open source: try it at Agent R Q dot com.
